title: migrate silently overwrites an existing roadmap

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`migrator.write` rewrites `config.json` and `index.json` unconditionally. `cmd_migrate`
has no `already_exists` guard and no `--force`, unlike `init`.

    $ slicer add "my existing item"; slicer add "another"
    $ slicer migrate --from docs/slices
    wrote 6 files ...
    $ slicer list      # the two items are gone, replaced by the migration

One mistaken `migrate` in an initialized project destroys the current roadmap, and leaves
any slice files whose ids are not in the migrated index as orphans. `.slicer/` is
committed so git is the recovery, but the tool should refuse, not rely on that.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `migrate` into a project that already has items refuses, exit 2, nothing written.
2. `migrate --force` proceeds.
3. `migrate` into a fresh `init` (empty index) still works without `--force`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Refuse when the index already has items unless `--force` is passed, the way `init`
refuses an existing config. An empty initialized project is fine — that is the normal
"init then migrate" path. Name the guard in the message and point at `--force`.

**Not in this slice:** merging a migration into an existing roadmap; refuse-or-replace is
the honest choice.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `migrate` over a non-empty project refuses; over an empty one it proceeds.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit: the guard in `cmd_migrate`, `--force` on the subparser, and the guard
tests in `tests/test_migrate.py`.
